newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trading booms as bank rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trading booms as bank rates fall.

text.p: Demand for Nigerian shares is at a record high causing prices to soar as investors continue to pump more funds into the stock market, operators said on Tuesday.
They said the fall in interest rates was partly responsible, forcing depositors to seek better returns elsewhere.
"There is much liquidity in the banks now because people are not borrowing money," Mike Itegboje, chief executive officer of TRW Stockbrokers, told Reuters.
The rates have fallen to as low as five percent from 13 percent at the beginning of this year.
Interest rates were fixed at 21 percent at the start of 1996 but government, bowing to pressures from the World Bank and the gradual stability of the economy, decided to uncap them.
"The capital market seems to be the area where the returns are rosier," said Itegboje, adding that investors seeking to diversify were responsible for the boom in stocks.
Improved trading results by companies was also responsible for the bullish nature of the market, analysts said.

"Companies doing well are appreciating as well as those investors think are going to post better results," one said, adding: "Things have improved since last year when many companies suffered poor returns."
Leading companies in the manufacturing and banking sectors which announced improved results are currently among current top performers on the stock exchange.

Shares of Cadbury and Union Bank, two leading stocks whose 1996 results are currently making waves, had almost doubled to 41.30 naira and 11.30 naira, respectively, by Monday against 21.40 naira and 6.00 naira in January.
Broker Dupe Dada of Prominent Securities said: "Some smaller companies are receiving attention as well because some investors believe they will appreciate in future."

Dealers said trading in the stock market would continue to be bullish unless the economy, recovering gradually from the political crisis of an annulled 1993 presidential election, sttumbled into another crisis.
Analysts predicted more companies would come out of recession as the government continued with its policy of guided deregulation which it introduced in the 1995 fiscal budget.
Share prices were expected to further rise, they said.
The stock market's capitalisation on Thursday was 311 billion naira, up from 285.6 billion naira at the end-1996.
